images.caption:
Thunderstorms during the North American Monsoon as seen from El Cajon, California. This is a common sight from southern California during the monsoon season. The monsoon pushes up against the Peninsular Range but only rarely manages to push over the mountains to the coastal strip. During the monsoon season southern Californians have a spectacular view of the thunderstorms only a half-hour's drive away. The storms reach the coastal strip only about once a season.
This photograph was created from 4 images stitched together with The Panorama Factory v.4. The image was cropped and reduced to 800 pixels vertically for convenient viewing.

Note: This is a replacement for Image for North American Monsoon 20060701.jpg, which was shown in the North American Monsoon section of the Monsoon article. I noted that I wanted to take a better picture. It took over two years but here it is. I took several panoramas of the monsoon on August 8, 2008. I think this is the best one and I doubt I will ever get a better shot.

images.filename: San Francisco de la Sierra Canyon 270.jpg
images.caption:
270° Panorama of a river-carved canyon in the Sierra de San Francisco mountain range, in the northern region of Baja California Sur state on the Baja California Peninsula, Mexico. 
The canyon valley and river drops towards the village of Santa Teresita on the left.
The far right leads to the mountain village of San Francisco de la Sierra, the locale of numerous prehistoric rock art pictographs, the Rock Paintings of Sierra de San Francisco.
The flora (plants) is of the Baja California Desert ecoregion. The Sierra de San Francisco are in the Peninsular Ranges system.
images.alt:
270° Panorama of a river-carved canyon in the Sierra de San Francisco mountain range, in the northern region of Baja California Sur state on the Baja California Peninsula, Mexico.
